title: Service Interruption Telemetry & QoS Signer Spec
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This design spec describes the Service Interruption Telemetry (SIT) pipeline and the QoS Signer component. The goal is to provide a standardized, low-latency, auditable signal that downstream routing, billing, and customer-facing dashboards can consume to make deterministic fidelity and fallback decisions during partial outages or capacity pressure events.

Intended audience:
- Runtime engineers
- Observability & SRE teams
- Product teams owning SLA behavior and customer communication
- Customer Success for playbook alignment

Problem statement:
- During partial infrastructure degradation (GPU exhaustion, regional network blips, overloaded KV caches), downstream services need a consistent, authenticated, and lightweight telemetry signal that summarizes the operational state for a tenant/route/model pair.
- Current signals are ad-hoc: a mix of traces, per-request metrics, and expensive cross-service joins that are too slow or inconsistent for fast routing decisions.
- Lack of a signed, low-latency service-state signal causes variability in fallback behavior across components and unclear customer-facing explanations for fidelity changes.

Goals:
1) Define a compact telemetry envelope (SIT envelope) that is produced near the serving runtime and signed by a QoS Signer service.
2) Provide a TLS-backed, key-rotatable signing mechanism so downstream services can validate authenticity without heavy RPCs.
3) Ensure the SIT pipeline meets latency and delivery budgets suitable for real-time routing (target 95th percentile < 25ms from event to envelope availability in the regional cache).
4) Map SIT states to deterministic routing and fidelity policies across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
5) Provide backward-compatible telemetry for dashboards and billing so incident explanations and cost attributions remain accurate.

Non-goals:
- This spec does not replace full distributed tracing or long-term audit logs. It is a short-lived operational signal intended for routing and immediate decisioning.
- This spec does not define UI changes for customer-facing console; integration guidance will be provided in a separate doc.

High-level architecture:
- Serving runtime (inference-exec) emits a lightweight event to the regional signal-hub when it observes threshold-crossing conditions (queue depth, token-lag, eviction-rate, GPU-temp).
- signal-hub aggregates events into a per-tenant/per-route/per-model SIT envelope with a short TTL (default 30s).
- qos-signer pulls canonical SIT envelopes from the signal-hub, attaches a signed header/payload using the tenant-specific signing key, and writes the signed envelope to the regional fast-cache (redis-cluster) and to a durable high-throughput ingest (kinesis/topic) for auditing.
- downstream components (fallback-router, cost-manager, console-telemetry) validate signatures via public-key endpoints and apply policy.

Component definitions and responsibilities:
- inference-exec (serving runtime): Emits raw condition events. Responsible for rate-limiting and ensuring per-request overhead < 1ms.
- signal-hub: Stateless aggregator service that normalizes events, collapses duplicates, and enforces a max-envelope-size of 2KB. Exposes a /sits/latest/{tenant}/{route}/{model} endpoint.
- qos-signer: Responsible for signing SIT envelopes with short-lived keys. Supports key rotation and multi-key signing for migration.
- regional-fast-cache: Read-optimized store for real-time retrieval (TTL configurable).
- audit-stream: Durable event stream for post-facto analysis and billing.

SIT envelope schema (compact form):
- List of fields below for implementation. Envelopes must be JSON, then base64-encoded when embedded in headers. Example: SIT: eyJ2IjoiMSIsInQiOjE2Mjc0...

Table: SIT envelope fields
| field | type | description | sample | retention / TTL |
| v | string | envelope version | "1" | n/a |
| ts | iso8601 | event timestamp | "2026-05-19T15:12:02Z" | TTL window |
| tenant_id | string | tenant canonical id | "t-42b9" | TTL window |
| route | string | customer route id | "/v1/chat/completions" | TTL window |
| model | string | model variant id | "rw-instruct-7b-q4" | TTL window |
| state | enum | operational state (OK, THROTTLED, DEGRADED, EVICTING, UNAVAILABLE) | "DEGRADED" | TTL window |
| score | number | 0..1 float indicating severity | "0.73" | TTL window |
| causes | list<string> | short cause tokens | ["queue_depth", "kv_eviction"] | TTL window |
| avg_latency_ms | number | rolling 95th latency in ms | "187.4" | TTL window |
| tokens_dropped | int | tokens dropped rate per sec | "12" | TTL window |
| sig_kid | string | signing key id used by qos-signer | "k-2026-05-01-1" | n/a |
| sig | base64 | signature of canonicalized envelope | "MEYCIQ..." | n/a |

Signing & verification protocol:
1) Canonicalization: signal-hub canonicalizes JSON fields (alphabetical keys, stable numeric formatting) and computes SHA-256 digest.
2) Signing: qos-signer signs the digest with tenant-scoped signing private key (RSA-PSS or ECDSA P-256 — implementation to be decided in step 1 of rollout). The signer returns sig_kid and sig.
3) Verification: downstream components obtain tenant public keys from the KeyRegistry service (cached with 1h TTL) and validate signature.
4) Key rotation: QoS Signer supports overlapping trust windows; signer must maintain an index of active key ids. Keys rotate every 7 days by default for hosted tenants; on-prem customers may configure longer windows.

Performance targets and SLOs:
- End-to-end envelope availability: 95th percentile < 25ms; 99th percentile < 100ms for regional reads.
- Signature verification latency budget: verification < 5ms for cached keys; < 50ms for cold public key fetch.
- Envelope TTL: default 30s; configurable per-tenant (min 10s, max 5m).
- Delivery durability: audit-stream ingestion SLO of 99.9% for successfully persisted envelopes.
- Operational cost cap: per-tenant telemetry ingestion must not exceed 0.5% of serving requests cost (target).

Routing policy mapping (examples):
- OK: No action.
- THROTTLED (score 0.4 - 0.7): apply adaptive-batching with reduced concurrency; surface transparent "graceful degrade" message to console.
- DEGRADED (score >0.7): route to lower-fidelity variant or enable quantization fallback; if tenant has Dedicated license and warm-capacity, attempt warm-capacity burst path.
- UNAVAILABLE: immediate fallback to best-effort variant or queued retry policy.

Configuration & runtime knobs (table):
| config_key | default | description | owner_service |
| sit.default_ttl_s | "30" | SIT envelope TTL in seconds | signal-hub |
| sit.aggregation_window_ms | "200" | window for collapsing duplicates | signal-hub |
| sit.max_emit_per_min | "60" | max SIT emits per tenant per minute | inference-exec |
| qos.signer.key_rotation_days | "7" | days between default key rotations for hosted | qos-signer |
| qos.verifier.cache_ttl_s | "3600" | public key cache TTL for verification | fallback-router / cost-manager |

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Detection: If frontend alerts show a sustained rise in sit.DEGRADED signals > 5% tenants in region, open incident.
2) Triage: Query audit-stream for envelopes with ts window and aggregate causes. Use the SIT playback tool to rehydrate envelopes for affected tenants.
3) Mitigation: If GPU pressure observed, reduce default max_concurrency via control plane or scale warm capacity. If signer's latency increases above 50ms, fail-open to unsigned local-envelope with special header X-SIT-UNSIGNED: true and page qos-signer on-call.
4) Customer communication: Use standardized template (appendix) to explain fidelity changes and duration.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (lab): Implement signal-hub and local signed envelopes in staging; run synthetic fault-injection to verify canonicalization and signing.
- Phase 1 (opt-in tenants): Enable SIT for 5% developer tenants and one mid-market customer; verify receiver integration with fallback-router and cost-manager.
- Phase 2 (gradual region rollout): Increase to 50% regional coverage; enable audit-stream retention and developer console annotations.
- Phase 3 (global default): Turn on for all hosted tenants; enable key rotation automation and create migration guide for Dedicated/Private customers.

Backwards compatibility & migration notes for Dedicated/Private:
- For Dedicated clusters we will ship a local qos-signer sidecar that uses on-prem KeyRegistry or HSM.
- Private deployments must set qos.signer.key_rotation_days to match their compliance windows and provide public key endpoints.
- Compatibility shim: if downstream cannot verify signature, fall back to an unsigned SIT envelope with header X-SIT-UNVERIFIED and a high-visibility metric sit.unverified_count incremented per tenant.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Private key storage: Hosted private keys are stored in KMS with strict RBAC. Key access logs must be routed to compliance S3 and retain 12 months.
- Sensitive fields: SIT envelopes must not include PII. tenant_id is opaque and maps to customer metadata in separate service.
- Replay protection: the ts field + short TTL reduce replay risk; signers reject envelopes with ts outside a configurable skew (default 5s).

API examples:
- Fetch latest SIT envelope (signal-hub):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://signal-hub.us-east-1.internal/sits/latest/t-42b9/%2Fv1%2Fchat%2Fcompletions/rw-instruct-7b-q4

- Example canonical envelope (pre-signing):
  {
    "avg_latency_ms":187.4,
    "causes":["queue_depth","kv_eviction"],
    "model":"rw-instruct-7b-q4",
    "route":"/v1/chat/completions",
    "score":0.73,
    "state":"DEGRADED",
    "tenant_id":"t-42b9",
    "ts":"2026-05-19T15:12:02Z",
    "v":"1"
  }

- Example header after signing:
  SIT: eyJ2IjoiMSIsInQiOiIyMDI2L...
  X-SIT-SIG-KID: k-2026-05-01-1

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Metrics to emit: sit.emitted_total, sit.signed_total, sit.verification_failures, sit.unverified_count, sit.latency_p95, sit.audit_ingest_failures.
- Dashboards: regional SIT health, tenant blast radius, signature verification heatmap, SIT-causes waterfall (queue_depth, kv_eviction, gpu_temp).

Open design decisions (to be resolved before Phase 1):
- Choice of signing algorithm (ECDSA P-256 vs RSA-PSS). Proposal: ECDSA for payload size and verification speed; validate against HSM support.
- Default TTL tuning: 30s chosen conservatively; run experiments to test 10s and 60s tradeoffs.
- Key rotation cadence for enterprise vs hosted customers.

Appendices:
A) Customer-facing fidelity template (snippet):
"We observed a transient service degradation affecting model responses for route /v1/chat/completions. As a result, responses were served at reduced fidelity for approximately 12 minutes. We reverted to normal fidelity at 15:25 UTC. If you need a post-incident export of SIT envelopes for your tenant, contact Support."

B) Implementation checklist:
- [ ] signal-hub API and aggregation logic implemented
- [ ] qos-signer MVP with key rotation and KMS integration
- [ ] regional-fast-cache read path and TTL enforcement
- [ ] audit-stream ingestion and retention policy
- [ ] fallback-router verification integration and policy mapping
- [ ] dashboards and alert rules created
